keyword: has iran opened the strait of hormuz

verifications.claim: As of April 8, 2026, Iran has agreed to a conditional, two-week ceasefire with the U.S.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Trump said he had agreed to suspend planned bombing for two weeks if Iran agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (R1); President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he agreed to suspend planned attacks... for two weeks, subject to... Iran agreeing to the COMPLETE... OPENING of the Strait of Hormuz (R2); US and Iran agreed to a conditional two-week ceasefire deal that includes the reopening... (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm conditional two-week ceasefire agreement around early April 2026 (e.g., April 7), but no exact mention of 'April 8'; date is close but less precise.

verifications.claim: The ceasefire includes allowing ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz after weeks of closure
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: suspend planned bombing for two weeks if Iran agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (R1); agreeing to the COMPLETE, IMMEDIATE, and SAFE OPENING of the Strait of Hormuz (R2); cease-fire deal... Iran allow... vessels to proceed... through the Strait of Hormuz (R4); Iran has responded... by effectively blocking traffic through the strait (R5)
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly state the ceasefire is tied to reopening the Strait after prior closure/disruption.

verifications.claim: The reopening is part of a deal following threats of massive U.S. strikes
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Trump set a deadline for Iran to fully reopen... or face broad strikes on its critical infrastructure. Hours before the deadline expired... (R1); backing off his shocking threats to imminently order the destruction of Iran’s “whole civilization” (R2); threatened to start wiping out Iran’s “whole civilization” if it did not allow... (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly link the deal/reopening to Trump's prior threats of massive strikes on infrastructure.

verifications.claim: Safe passage is now coordinated with Iran's military
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be possible via coordination with Iran's Armed Forces (R1, R3); via coordination with Iran’s Armed Forces (R2); safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be possible” if coordinated with Iran’s military (R4); safe passage... via coordination with Iran’s Armed Forces (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly quote or paraphrase the coordination requirement for safe passage.

verifications.claim: Iran's Foreign Minister stated that safe passage is possible
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi then said that "safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be possible..." (R1, R3); ships will be able to safely pass through the strait... (R2); safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be possible (R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct quotes from Iran's FM stating safe passage is possible.

verifications.claim: Iran's Foreign Minister stated that safe passage is only via coordination with Iran's Armed Forces
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be possible via coordination with Iran's Armed Forces..." (R1, R3); “via coordination with Iran’s Armed Forces... (R2, R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: FM states it 'will be possible via coordination,' implying that's the method, but does not explicitly say 'only.'

verifications.claim: Iran's Foreign Minister stated that safe passage is based on technical limitations
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: ...via coordination with Iran's Armed Forces and with due consideration of technical limitations (R1, R3); with due consideration of technical limitations (R2); with due consideration of technical limitations (R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: FM mentions 'due consideration of technical limitations' as part of the condition, but not that passage 'is based on' them.

verifications.claim: The 10-point proposal to end the conflict is for two weeks
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: We received a 10 point proposal from Iran, and believe it is a workable basis on which to negotiate... a two week period will allow the Agreement to be finalized (R2); agreed to base the next two weeks of talks on a 10-point plan Iran submitted (R4)
verifications.reasoning: The 10-point proposal is a basis for long-term peace negotiations; the two-week duration is for the ceasefire/negotiation period, not the proposal itself.

verifications.claim: Prior to this agreement, Iran had effectively blocked traffic through the Strait of Hormuz for over a month
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Shipping traffic... has been effectively halted since the war began (R4); Iran has responded to strikes by effectively blocking traffic through the strait (R5); disruption of the vital maritime passageway... through which some 20% of the world's oil supply is shipped (R1)
verifications.reasoning: War began Feb. 28 (~5-6 weeks to April); sources confirm effective block/halt of traffic prior to agreement.

verifications.claim: The decision followed a 5 PM deadline set by President Trump
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: 10 a.m. ET deadline (R1); The 8 p.m. ET deadline — which Trump set Sunday (R2); 8 p.m. Eastern time deadline (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention Trump deadlines (e.g., 8 p.m. ET, 10 a.m. ET) but not a 5 PM deadline; specific time contradicts referenced deadlines.

verifications.claim: President Trump threatened severe retaliation against Iran
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Trump threatened... If any of these ships come anywhere close to our BLOCKADE, they will be immediately ELIMINATED (R1); threats to imminently order the destruction of Iran’s “whole civilization”... “A whole civilization will die tonight (R2); face broad strikes on its critical infrastructure (R3); threatened to start wiping out Iran’s “whole civilization” (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct references to Trump's threats of severe/massive retaliation/strikes.
